newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold volume halved on weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold volume halved on weak demand.

text.p: Volume halved on Istanbul's gold exchange on Tuesday as demand shrank due to lower gold prices on the free market, dealers said.
Traded volume was 448 kg, down sharply from Monday's 922. Sixty-four percent of the total turnover was in lira terms.
Prices were mixed. Gold closed at $381.50 an ounce compared to $382.30 on Friday, when the last trade in dollar terms was made.
It jumped by 9,950 lira on the bourse from Monday's close to end at 1,162,200 lira per gramme due to a weak lira which finished at 94,450 against the dollar versus yesterday's 94,000.
"Gold trade was weak today because of high prices prompted by the lira's fall. Seasonal demand has also passed and volume cannot reach the levels seen in the active summer season," said one dealer.
